alt: A block diagram of a computer. An Input block on the left has an arrow to a large CPU block in the middle. The CPU block contains two smaller boxes labelled A and B. An arrow runs from the CPU down to a block labelled C, and another arrow runs from the CPU right to an Output block.

Three database tables. STUDENT has the fields Student_ID, Name and Grade, with rows S001 Amali 11, S002 Kasun 10, and S003 Nimal 11. SUBJECT has the fields Subject_ID and Subject_name, with rows SU01 ICT and SU02 Maths. ENROLMENT has the fields Student_ID, Subject_ID and Marks, with rows S001 SU01 78, S002 SU02 65, and S001 SU02 81.

A flowchart. Start, then Input N, then a process box setting S to 0 and I to 1. A decision box asks "Is I > N?". On No, a process box sets S to S + I and I to I + 1, and the flow returns to just below Input N. On Yes, the flow goes to Output S and then End.

A logic circuit with three inputs A, B and C, and one output Q. A and B go into a two-input AND gate. C goes into a NOT gate. The output of the AND gate and the output of the NOT gate are the two inputs of a two-input OR gate, whose output is Q.
A logic circuit with two inputs A and B and one output Q. A and B are the inputs of a NAND gate. The output of that NAND gate is the single input of a NOT gate, and the output of the NOT gate is Q.

A logic circuit with two inputs A and B and one output Q. A and B are the inputs of an OR gate. B also branches to the input of a NOT gate. The OR gate output and the NOT gate output are the two inputs of an AND gate, whose output is Q.
An eight-column place-value frame. The headings are the powers of two from 2 to the 7 down to 2 to the 0. The single row of digits beneath them reads, from left to right, 1 0 1 1 0 1 0 1.
A spreadsheet segment. Cell A1 contains Rate and cell B1 contains 15. Row 2 holds the headings Hours in A2 and Pay in B2. Cell A3 contains 8 and cell A4 contains 6. Column B is empty in rows 3 and 4.
A spreadsheet segment. Row 1 holds the headings Item, Qty, Price and Total in columns A to D. Row 2 is Pen, 12, 25. Row 3 is Book, 5, 120. Row 4 is Bag, 2, 850. Column D is empty in rows 2 to 4.
A network diagram. One long horizontal cable runs across the diagram, labelled backbone cable. Four computers labelled PC1 to PC4 each drop a short vertical cable down onto that single shared cable.
A network diagram. Five computers labelled PC1 to PC5 are arranged in a closed loop, each one cabled to exactly two neighbours, so the cabling forms a single unbroken ring with no central device.
A network diagram. Five computers labelled PC1 to PC5 each connect by a single separate cable to one central switch. No computer connects directly to another.
A truth table with columns A, B and Q. The rows are: A 0, B 0, Q 1; A 0, B 1, Q 1; A 1, B 0, Q 1; A 1, B 1, Q 0.
